title: Filings Unit Memorandum — Certificate Exposure Charge on an Owner Auto Policy Reinstatement with Lapse
content:
**Charge.** On a reinstatement with lapse of an Owner Auto Policy term, a certificate exposure charge is added to the reinstatement fee. It turns on how the certificate backed by the term, an SR-22 or FR-44 filing under the Financial Responsibility Filings (SR-22 / FR-44), stood with the state while coverage lapsed. The charge prices a liability that the lapse days carried no premium for and that the certificate's filing fee does not price. The certificate is read as it stood on the reinstatement effective date, so neither a certificate filed after that date nor an SR-26 transmitted after it changes the reading.

| Certificate standing | Charge added |
|---|---|
| Kept in force through the lapse: standing filed on the reinstatement effective date, with no SR-26 transmitted on or before it. The company stays bound to the state for every lapse day. A certificate stands filed on that date when the certificate entered first with status filed has its filed date on or before that date, or the certificate entered first with status cancellation filed has its filed date on or before that date and its SR-26 date after it | 5.00 |
| SR-26 transmitted on or before the reinstatement effective date (status cancellation filed, SR-26 date on or before that date), with a certificate end date on or after that date. The company stays bound for part of the lapse | 3.00 |
| Ended before coverage was restored (certificate end date before the reinstatement effective date). A new filing, charged under its own fee, must replace it | nothing |
| No certificate | nothing |

**Records read.** For each Financial Responsibility Filings (SR-22 / FR-44) certificate backed by the term: its status (filed, or cancellation filed once the SR-26 has been transmitted), filed date, SR-26 date and certificate end date. The certificate entered first is used when several share a status. The term's reinstatement effective date is also read.

**Boundary (hypothetical).** The reinstatement effective date is the 20th.
- SR-26 dated the 15th, certificate end date the 20th: adds 3.00.
- SR-26 dated the 15th, certificate end date the 19th: adds nothing.
- SR-26 dated the 22nd on a certificate filed before the 20th: it stood filed on the 20th, so it adds 5.00.
